## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(here)
library(scales)

library(tidyverse)
library(bayesrules)
library(janitor)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(plotly)
library(e1071)

library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
# Waikiki Roughwater Swim results scraper (1970–2015, waikikiroughwaterswim.com)
#
# What it does:
#   * Reads the year links from the official results index page
#   * On each year's page, takes the OVERALL results table (falls back to the
#     AGE GROUP table when a year has no overall table, e.g. 1970)
#   * Keeps every value exactly as text, as shown on the page (no type
#     conversion, no filling, no corrections)
#   * Adds only provenance columns: year, source_url, source_table, and (for the
#     age-group fallback) the section label printed on the page
#   * Writes one combined CSV plus a log that lets you check row counts against
#     the "Total Finishers" figure each page reports
#
# Required packages: install.packages(c("rvest", "dplyr", "purrr", "stringr", "readr"))

library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

# ---- 1. Build the year URLs directly ----------------------------------------
# Every year 1970–2015 on the site uses the same address pattern, so the URLs
# are built directly rather than read from the index page (reading the index
# from R did not return the links). 2016+ results are on pseresults.com and
# are not HTML tables, so they are not included here.
years <- 1970:2015
year_urls <- tibble(
  year = years,
  url  = paste0("https://waikikiroughwaterswim.com/results-", years, "/")
)

message(nrow(year_urls), " year pages to scrape")  # should say 46

# ---- 2. Helpers -------------------------------------------------------------
squish_df <- function(df) {
  as.data.frame(lapply(df, function(x) str_squish(as.character(x))),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

first_col_has <- function(tbl, key) any(str_squish(tbl[[1]]) == key)

# Use the row whose first cell equals `header_key` as the header; drop anything
# above it, repeated header rows, and fully blank rows.
tidy_table <- function(raw, header_key) {
  m <- squish_df(raw)
  hdr <- which(m[[1]] == header_key)
  if (length(hdr) == 0) return(NULL)
  header <- as.character(unlist(m[hdr[1], ]))
  body <- m[-seq_len(hdr[1]), , drop = FALSE]
  names(body) <- make.unique(ifelse(header == "", "unnamed", header))
  body <- body[body[[1]] != header_key, , drop = FALSE]
  body <- body[apply(body, 1, function(r) any(r != "")), , drop = FALSE]
  body
}

# Age-group tables interleave section labels ("Male 15 – 18") and "NONE" rows.
# Section labels are moved into a `section` column (text copied from the page);
# rows whose only content is "NONE" are dropped (they are not swimmers).
tidy_age_group <- function(raw) {
  df <- tidy_table(raw, "Division Place")
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  others <- df[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  is_section <- df[[1]] != "" & apply(others, 1, function(r) all(r == ""))
  labels <- c(NA_character_, df[[1]][is_section])
  df$section <- labels[cumsum(is_section) + 1]
  df <- df[!is_section, , drop = FALSE]
  vals <- df[, setdiff(names(df), "section"), drop = FALSE]
  is_none <- apply(vals, 1, function(r) all(r[r != ""] == "NONE"))
  df[!is_none, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Column names -> snake_case; "1971 Group" etc. -> year_group so years line up.
standardize_names <- function(df) {
  n <- str_to_lower(names(df))
  n <- str_replace(n, "^\\d{4} group$", "year_group")
  n <- str_replace_all(n, "[^a-z0-9]+", "_")
  names(df) <- str_remove_all(n, "^_|_$")
  df
}

# "Total Finishers" as printed in the page's statistics table (for checking).
get_total_finishers <- function(tables) {
  for (t in tables) {
    m <- as.matrix(squish_df(t))
    idx <- which(m == "Total Finishers", arr.ind = TRUE)
    if (nrow(idx) > 0 && idx[1, 2] < ncol(m)) return(m[idx[1, 1], idx[1, 2] + 1])
  }
  NA_character_
}

# ---- 3. Scrape one year -----------------------------------------------------
scrape_year <- function(year, url) {
  message("Scraping ", year)
  Sys.sleep(1)  # be polite to the server
  
  out <- tryCatch({
    tables <- read_html(url) |>
      html_elements("table") |>
      html_table(header = FALSE, convert = FALSE)
    
    overall_idx <- which(map_lgl(tables, first_col_has, "Overall Place"))
    ag_idx      <- which(map_lgl(tables, first_col_has, "Division Place"))
    
    if (length(overall_idx) > 0) {
      df <- tidy_table(tables[[overall_idx[1]]], "Overall Place"); used <- "overall"
    } else if (length(ag_idx) > 0) {
      df <- tidy_age_group(tables[[ag_idx[1]]]); used <- "age_group"
    } else {
      df <- NULL; used <- NA_character_
    }
    
    if (!is.null(df) && nrow(df) > 0) {
      df <- standardize_names(df) |>
        mutate(year = year, source_url = url, source_table = used, .before = 1)
    }
    
    list(
      data = df,
      log = tibble(year = year, url = url,
                   status = if (is.null(df)) "no results table found" else "ok",
                   table_used = used,
                   rows_extracted = if (is.null(df)) 0L else nrow(df),
                   total_finishers_reported = get_total_finishers(tables))
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(data = NULL,
         log = tibble(year = year, url = url, status = paste("error:", conditionMessage(e)),
                      table_used = NA_character_, rows_extracted = 0L,
                      total_finishers_reported = NA_character_))
  })
  out
}

# ---- 4. Run and save --------------------------------------------------------
results <- map2(year_urls$year, year_urls$url, scrape_year)

all_data   <- bind_rows(compact(map(results, "data")))
scrape_log <- bind_rows(map(results, "log"))

# na = "NA" marks columns that did not exist for a given year; cells that were
# blank on the page stay as empty strings "", so the two are distinguishable.
write_csv(all_data,   "waikiki_rws_results_1970_2015.csv", na = "NA")
write_csv(scrape_log, "waikiki_rws_scrape_log.csv")

print(scrape_log, n = Inf)

# To read back without losing the blank-vs-missing distinction:
# d <- read_csv("waikiki_rws_results_1970_2015.csv",
#               col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = "NA")
```

```{r}
library(rvest)

inspect_page <- function(year) {
  url <- paste0("https://waikikiroughwaterswim.com/results-", year, "/")
  pg  <- read_html(url)
  tabs <- html_elements(pg, "table")
  cat("\n=====", year, ":", length(tabs), "table(s)\n")
  for (i in seq_along(tabs)) {
    t <- html_table(tabs[[i]], header = FALSE, convert = FALSE)
    cat("-- table", i, "(", nrow(t), "rows )\n")
    print(head(t, 4))
  }
  embeds <- html_attr(html_elements(pg, "iframe, embed, object"), "src")
  links  <- html_attr(html_elements(pg, "a"), "href")
  files  <- links[str_detect(links, "(?i)\\.(pdf|xlsx?|csv)$|docs\\.google|drive\\.google")]
  cat("embedded:", if (length(embeds)) embeds else "none", "\n")
  cat("file links:", if (length(files)) files else "none", "\n")
}

walk(c(1989, 2003, 2008, 2014), inspect_page)
```

```{r}
# Dump every table from the Waikiki Roughwater results pages that the main
# script could not read (1989, 2003–2014), one CSV per table, so each year's
# layout can be checked before anything is merged into the main dataset.
#
# Values are kept exactly as text, as shown on the page. The only changes:
#   * blank rows and repeated header rows are dropped
#   * a row whose only content is its first cell (e.g. "MALE OVERALL RESULTS",
#     "FEMALE AGE GROUP: FIN") is treated as a section label and moved into a
#     `section` column for the rows under it
#   * if a table has no header row, its columns are named x1, x2, ... (no names
#     are guessed)

library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

years   <- c(1989, 2003:2004, 2006:2014)
out_dir <- "raw_tables"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# A header row has at least 3 filled cells and mentions "place" or "name".
is_header_row <- function(r) {
  sum(r != "") >= 3 && any(str_detect(r, "(?i)place|name"))
}

tidy_any_table <- function(raw) {
  m <- as.data.frame(lapply(raw, \(x) str_squish(as.character(x))),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  m <- m[apply(m, 1, \(r) any(r != "")), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(m) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  hdr_idx <- which(apply(m, 1, is_header_row))
  if (length(hdr_idx) > 0) {
    header <- as.character(unlist(m[hdr_idx[1], ]))
    is_hdr <- apply(m, 1, \(r) identical(as.character(r), header))
    m <- m[!is_hdr, , drop = FALSE]
    nm <- ifelse(header == "", paste0("x", seq_along(header)), header)
  } else {
    nm <- paste0("x", seq_len(ncol(m)))
  }
  names(m) <- make.unique(nm)
  
  if (ncol(m) >= 2) {
    others     <- m[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    is_section <- m[[1]] != "" & apply(others, 1, \(r) all(r == ""))
    labels     <- c(NA_character_, m[[1]][is_section])
    m$section  <- labels[cumsum(is_section) + 1]
    m <- m[!is_section, , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    m$section <- NA_character_
  }
  list(data = m, header_found = length(hdr_idx) > 0)
}

dump_page <- function(year) {
  url <- paste0("https://waikikiroughwaterswim.com/results-", year, "/")
  message("Reading ", year)
  Sys.sleep(1)
  tables <- tryCatch(
    read_html(url) |> html_elements("table") |>
      html_table(header = FALSE, convert = FALSE),
    error = \(e) { message("  ", year, ": ", conditionMessage(e)); list() }
  )
  imap_dfr(tables, \(raw, i) {
    res <- tidy_any_table(raw)
    if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
    f <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%d_table%d.csv", year, i))
    write_csv(res$data, f, na = "NA")
    tibble(
      year = year, table = i,
      rows = nrow(res$data),
      header_found = res$header_found,
      columns  = paste(setdiff(names(res$data), "section"), collapse = " | "),
      sections = paste(unique(na.omit(res$data$section)), collapse = " | "),
      file = f
    )
  })
}

index <- map_dfr(years, dump_page)
write_csv(index, file.path(out_dir, "_index.csv"))
print(select(index, year, table, rows, header_found, columns), n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

```{r}
# Add 1989 and 2003–2014 (from the raw_tables/ CSVs written by
# dump_other_formats.R) to the main 1970–2002 dataset.
#
# Values stay exactly as on the pages. Column NAMES are standardized only where
# the meaning is unambiguous (e.g. "FName" / "FIRST NAME" -> first_name).
# Columns whose meaning varies by year are left under their own names; in
# particular "Place" is kept as `place` (NOT merged into overall_place), because
# in some years it may be place within sex rather than overall place.

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)

# ---- Which table to use for each year (edit here if you disagree) -----------
chosen <- tribble(
  ~year, ~table, ~note,
  1989, 1, "alphabetical listing with all columns",
  2003, 1, "age-group listing (table 2 is malformed: rows packed into one cell)",
  2004, 1, "",
  2006, 1, "",
  2007, 1, "CHECK: table 2 has the same 706 rows with Bib No and Age Group; unclear which column is overall place",
  2008, 1, "overall listing split by sex sections (see `section`); table 2 is a 100-row age-group list",
  2009, 1, "table 2 has no headers",
  2010, 2, "table 3 (930 rows, 1970s-2002 style columns) looks copied from another year; table 1 has no headers",
  2011, 1, "table 2 has the same columns and row count",
  2012, 1, "table 2 has the same columns and row count",
  2013, 1, "CHECK: table 2 has 923 rows (1 fewer); table 3 (26 rows) may be a fins division",
  2014, 2, "table 1 = women-only overall subset; table 3 (26 rows) = fins division"
)

# ---- Unambiguous column-name synonyms ---------------------------------------
std_names <- function(n) {
  n <- str_to_lower(n) |>
    str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]+", "_") |>
    str_remove_all("^_|_$")
  n <- recode(n,
              fname = "first_name", lname = "last_name",
              div_place = "division_place", div_plc = "division_place",
              divplace = "division_place",
              div = "division", age_group = "division",
              no = "bib", bib_no = "bib", number = "bib",
              over = "overall_place", sexpla = "sex_place"
  )
  make.unique(n, sep = "_")
}

# ---- Read the chosen tables -------------------------------------------------
extra <- pmap_dfr(chosen, \(year, table, note) {
  f <- file.path("raw_tables", sprintf("%d_table%d.csv", year, table))
  d <- read_csv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = "NA")
  names(d) <- std_names(names(d))
  d |>
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(year),
      source_url = paste0("https://waikikiroughwaterswim.com/results-", year, "/"),
      source_table = paste0("table ", table),
      .before = 1
    )
})

# ---- Combine with the main 1970–2002 file -----------------------------------
main <- read_csv("waikiki_rws_results_1970_2015.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = "NA") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

combined <- bind_rows(main, extra) |> arrange(year)

write_csv(combined, "waikiki_rws_results_combined.csv", na = "NA")

# ---- Checks -----------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Years present:", sort(unique(combined$year)), "\n")
cat("Columns:", names(combined), sep = "\n  ")

# Uses overall_place where it exists, otherwise `place`.
# Many duplicate places in a year usually means `place` restarts within each
# sex or section, i.e. it is not overall place for that year.
combined |>
  filter(year %in% chosen$year) |>
  mutate(p = suppressWarnings(as.integer(coalesce(overall_place, place)))) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    rows       = n(),
    max_place  = max(p, na.rm = TRUE),
    blank      = sum(is.na(p)),
    dup_places = sum(duplicated(p[!is.na(p)])),
    sections   = n_distinct(section, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```
